again/loop: A language model writes text one token at a time: run the model on the sequence so far, pick the next token, append it, and run again.
again/redo: Done plainly, every step runs the whole sequence, so every block computes every token's key and value again, though only one token is new.
again/same: And the old ones come out the same every time. With the causal mask, an earlier token never attends to a later one, so adding a token changes nothing before it.
again/count: Step one computes one key, step two computes two, up to T at step T. That adds up to T times T plus one, over two: for ten steps, fifty-five.
cache/keep: So keep them. The KV cache stores the keys and values of every token so far, in every block.
cache/step: Each step now computes a query, key and value for the newest token only, adds its key and value to the cache, and attends over everything stored.
cache/work: Ten steps compute ten keys instead of fifty-five. For a thousand tokens, a thousand instead of half a million.
cache/shape: In one block, after T tokens, the cached keys form a T by d array, and the values another, each growing by one row per step.
cache/memory: The price is memory: two times the blocks, times T, times d numbers, for every sequence being written.
